title: Choose the visual world
question: You pinned Swiss editorial / brutalist-tech, and a pinned brief beats the roll — so that world leads here, already raised by the roll's assigned direction and the challengers it beat. Lock it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Secure Delivery Datasheet
options.lineage: Swiss technical datasheet / component spec-sheet + supply-chain provenance seal
options.thesis: Your platform read as one engineered component datasheet, where every security property is a measured, stamped, verifiable spec — not a marketing adjective.
options.viewport: Near-black full-bleed. A giant tegas headline (role + the platform's one-sentence claim) pinned to a visible 12-column grid; a thin top rule carries micro-labels (name, role, a spec code, contact); one signal-orange accent marks the only 'live' element. Primary action (Contact / See the architecture) sits top-right on the rule line.
options.risk: Brutalist grids read cold or sterile if the type is set timidly or the single accent is used everywhere; the whole bet is nerve in the typography and restraint in the color.

raised.raise: Every security claim carries a provenance ritual: a spec starts UNVERIFIED and resolves to a stamped VERIFIED state on interaction, so the supply-chain story (sign -> scan -> admit) is literally the page's visual language.
Registration/certification marks and declared density tiers become real UI: section headers carry stamped spec codes, and dense regions shed ornament in named steps instead of just shrinking.
The one live accent element is a true metered 'signal strip' with weighted motion (pipeline stage / layer status), not an instant toggle, so the page has one honest moving instrument.
State changes are bound to exact pipeline events (push, build, SAST gate, sign, scan, admit) rather than applied as generic hover decoration.
Interactive demos give tactile, legible state feedback (a gate visibly latches, a rejected image visibly bounces) so the security mechanics are felt, not just labeled.

regions.label: top rule: name / role / spec code / contact

options.label: Hostile-Brand Info Noise
options.thesis: The same brutalist world turned to maximum energy: hazard grotesk, registration marks, and immaculate information density as the material itself.
options.viewport: Absolute black with one enormous condensed word shouting through layered warning glyphs, spec codes, and roundels gridded tight to the edge; the security layers read as stacked hazard classes.
options.case: Holds the audience-identification axis hard — this is brutalist-tech at full volume and DevSecOps people love it. Loses the clarity axis: density-as-material can bury the step-by-step pipeline flow a recruiter needs to follow, which is why it informs the lead rather than leading.
options.risk: Gorgeous but louder than it is legible; a non-specialist recruiter can bounce off pure information noise before they reach the proof.

options.label: Terminal / BBS Nightboard
options.lineage: dial-up ANSI bulletin board, CP437 character grid
options.thesis: The platform as a live terminal: pipeline logs stream in line-by-line at modem cadence, everything on a strict character grid.
options.viewport: Terminal-black 80-column grid; a title screen pours in at modem speed, numbered menu rows navigate sections, pipeline events land as live textmode events.
options.case: Wins the audience-identification axis (every security engineer lives in a terminal) and the git-push story is native here. Competitive, not winning: a full-terminal world fights the 'instantly legible to a non-specialist recruiter' requirement, so it stays an alternate rather than the build.
options.risk: Can read as retro-novelty and intimidate non-engineer recruiters; the live log motif is better borrowed into the datasheet than run as the whole page.

options.label: VU-Meter Bridge
options.lineage: recording-desk vu-meter bridge, true ballistic needles
options.case: Fuses weakly: a row of identical meters reads the 'room' at a glance but can't carry a 5-layer sequence or a push->deploy flow, which are the product's spine.
options.kept: True instrument ballistics — motion with mass and damping, never instant values.

options.label: Hand-Processed 16mm Film
options.lineage: hand-processed film strip, light leaks, emulsion artifacts
options.case: Fuses poorly: the audience doesn't identify DevSecOps with cinematography, and emulsion artifacts obscure rather than clarify a security flow.
options.kept: Artifacts bound to exact frames/events instead of a generic filter.

options.label: Skeuomorph Leather Studio
options.lineage: stitched-leather reading shelf, rendered physical objects
options.case: Fuses poorly and contradicts the pinned brutalist world outright: warm handmade objects are the opposite of a bank-grade engineered-security story.
options.kept: Tactile, legible state feedback on every control.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The default engineer-portfolio: dark theme, Inter, a timeline, neon-accent cards, a skills grid — executed cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: Centered hero with name + role, a horizontal tech-logo strip, scroll to a vertical timeline and a skills matrix.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from thousands of other engineer portfolios; safe, forgettable, and the opposite of the brief's 'no AI slop'.
